editorial:
Imagine your family gathering for Christmas, but instead of talking about presents, everyone is arguing about how broke they are. That is exactly where you find the Cosgroves. They are a messy group of people who decide the quickest way to fix their money problems is to rob a grumpy, lonely farmer named Charlie Bann. It feels like a typical heist movie at first, but the vibe quickly shifts from a funny family scrap to a wild ride where everything goes wrong. You will love how the movie blends dark humor with a sense of danger, making you laugh one minute and hold your breath the next.

The acting is spot on, especially the chemistry between the family members who just cannot stop bickering. The twists come out of nowhere and keep the story moving fast, though a few plot points feel a bit rushed toward the end. If you enjoy movies where regular people get in over their heads, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The big twist is that Charlie Bann was actually a retired government assassin who had been hiding from his past. He easily outsmarts the Cosgroves, turning the robbery into a deadly game of cat and mouse. In the final scenes, the family has to work together to escape his traps. Most of them make it out alive, but they end up losing all the money they stole, leaving them exactly where they started.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies and surprise twists.
